subject: Day 40: vaccine fever plan; acetaminophen dosing
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 40. The 2-month vaccine visit is two to four weeks out. Most infants run a low-grade fever and 24-48 hours of fussiness after the shots. Today is the day to plan around that window and confirm dosing.

Action items
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is booked; the vaccine list is HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1. AAP on immunizations: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Confirm infant acetaminophen and a digital rectal thermometer are on hand; ask the pediatrician at the visit to write the exact dose for Avi's current weight. AAP HealthyChildren on fever: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx
- Block out the day of the visit and the day after — do not schedule meetings or social plans.
- Anoushka's postpartum visit is two days away — confirm logistics. ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Spontaneous smiles; tracking 180 degrees; vowel coos consolidating.
- [low concern] Crying intensity at or near peak; hiccups; quiet startle.
- [monitor] No social smile by week 8 — note for the 2-month visit but not concerning today.
- [call within 24h] Sustained feeding refusal. Bloody-mucus stool. New murmur or blue color around lips during feeds.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Tummy time 30 minutes a day cumulative. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Hold him at a mirror for 60-90 seconds at his eye level.
- Take conversational turns with each vocalization. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Outdoor stroller walk for 20-30 minutes.

Upcoming
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 49: crying tapering noticeably.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
